accipiter, accipitris m.

noun, third declension

a hawk; any bird of prey of the falcon kind

Other words

  • plīpiō, plīpiāre — to cry (of a hawk)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 143

    Not in Lewis & Short; the vowel is left as Traupman marks it.

Examples

  • ōdimus accipitrem, quia vīvit semper in armīs

    we hate the hawk, because it lives always armedOv. Ars 2.147

  • Accipitrēs crōcitant.

    Hawks caw.Traupman 326

See also falcon, bird.
